answer: Latent behavior clustering. Each new identity must transact for seven days before full participation, and its transaction graph is compared against known clusters. An ember of shared device timing or funding path links accounts. The system groups identities whose action sequences overlap beyond chance, then applies a trellis of weighted features—transaction intervals, counterparty overlap, amount distributions—to score cluster cohesion. Accounts on the wrong side of a ledge of statistical improbability get throttled pending review.
